author: Karl Rock
description:
Step back 5,000 years into the heart of the Indus Valley Civilization at Mohenjo-Daro. This archaeological marvel, located in modern-day Pakistan, remains one of the world's earliest major urban centers. Known for its sophisticated city planning, advanced drainage systems, and standardized brick construction, the site offers a rare glimpse into a society that thrived when most of the world was still in its infancy. Even today, the scale of these ruins along the banks of the mighty Indus River is a testament to the ingenuity of the Bronze Age.

For those planning a visit to this UNESCO World Heritage site, the best time to explore is between November and February to avoid the intense desert heat. It is highly recommended to hire a local guide, as their insights into the site's complex layout and the mysterious, undeciphered Indus script add incredible depth to the experience.
